title: Complexe de De Rham à puissance divisée [conférence de 1976 à l’IHÉS] : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
This page is not a Grothendieck manuscript. It is the first page of a typed preprint, 'Points de Gorenstein d'un morphisme' by Manuela Stoia, with handwritten insertions: a reference, the second condition of the criterion, and some symbols. It is filed among the divided-power de Rham notes. The previous page is headed 'Feuille parasite', which suggests stray sheets mixed into the folder, and the next page returns to divided powers on Z/2-graded alternating algebras. Whose hand made the insertions is undetermined; they could be the author's own corrections.

Mathematics. A noetherian ring is Gorenstein if it has finite injective dimension (locally, in the usual convention). The paper uses this criterion: if A = B/I is a quotient of a regular local ring B, then A is Gorenstein if and only if Ext^q_B(A,B) = 0 for all q except one value q0, and Ext^{q0}_B(A,B) ≅ A. The single nonvanishing degree makes A Cohen–Macaulay with q0 = dim B − dim A. The condition Ext^{q0} ≅ A says the canonical module is free of rank 1, which is the Gorenstein condition.

Work over an algebraically closed field k, with algebraic varieties allowed to have nilpotents. Theorem: if f: X → Y is flat, the set G_f(X) = {x ∈ X : the fibre X_{f(x)} is Gorenstein at x} is open in X.

Proof begun. The question is local, so take X affine with a closed immersion j: X → A^n. Then f factors as π∘i, where i = (j×1_Y)∘Γ_f : X → A^n × Y is a closed immersion and π: A^n × Y → Y is the projection. Presumably the proof continues on later pages:
- Each fibre X_y is cut out of A^n_y, which is regular.
- The fibrewise criterion applies to the sheaves Ext^q_{O_{A^n×Y}}(O_X, O_{A^n×Y}).
- Flatness of X over Y gives base-change behaviour for these relative Ext sheaves.
- Semicontinuity or openness arguments then give openness of the locus.
This is the Gorenstein analogue of EGA IV 12.1.6–12.1.7 (openness of the Cohen–Macaulay locus of fibres for flat morphisms locally of finite presentation).
errors: No mathematical errors visible on this page. The criterion should be read for local rings, with q0 forced to equal dim B − dim A. Base change of Ext along the fibres is the delicate step, and it does not appear on this page.

ideas.what: Criterion: a quotient A of a regular local ring B is Gorenstein iff Ext^q_B(A,B) is concentrated in one degree q0 and Ext^{q0}_B(A,B) ≅ A
ideas.modern_name: Characterization of Gorenstein rings via the canonical module / dualizing complex
ideas.usually_credited_to: Bass (1963), Grothendieck (local duality), Hartshorne (Residues and Duality)
ideas.where_published: Local duality, SGA 2 / Hartshorne's Local Cohomology and Residues and Duality (in substance)

ideas.what: Openness of the locus of points where the fibre of a flat morphism is Gorenstein
ideas.modern_name: Openness of the Gorenstein locus of a flat morphism (Gorenstein morphisms)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Analogue of EGA IV 12.1.6 for Cohen–Macaulay; Gorenstein version in the literature of the 1970s (Stoia; Greco–Marinari) and the Stacks Project
ideas.where_published: EGA IV §12 for the analogous CM/regular properties; the Gorenstein case is not explicitly in EGA as far as I know

ideas.what: Factoring f through the graph and a closed immersion into A^n × Y to reduce to Ext over a smooth Y-scheme
ideas.modern_name: Standard local embedding of a morphism of finite type

deep.surprise_reason: This is a stray typed preprint by another mathematician (Manuela Stoia), unrelated to the surrounding divided-power material. It proves a standard openness result for the Gorenstein locus of fibres of a flat morphism, which is well known in the literature.
transcription_corrections: The page is typed (Stoia's preprint); the handwritten parts are insertions: 'et Ext^{q0}_B(A,B) ≅ A', the reference '[(3), prop. 1.3, ch 1, §1.4]', the citation '(4)', and the symbols O_{X,x}, G_f(X), j, π.
The circled symbol is π (projection), and the first map is Γ_f (graph morphism), as transcribed.
Bottom-left handwritten '215' is the archive page number.
